sections.html:
In Alabama's far northwest, on the banks of the Tennessee River, Colbert County has Tuscumbia as its seat and Muscle Shoals as its largest city. The Florence-Muscle Shoals metro, known locally as the Shoals, includes it. Cities are Muscle Shoals, Sheffield and Tuscumbia; towns are Cherokee, Leighton and Littleville.

Residents totaled 57,227 in 2020, up 5.1 percent from 54,428 in 2010, with 59,474 estimated for 2025. The housing count was 27,666 units for 24,425 households, and 11.7 percent of units stood empty. Homeowners account for 69.1 percent of occupied homes and renters 30.9 percent, while rental vacancy is 7.7 percent. City dwellers make up 59.7 percent of the population and rural residents 40.3 percent. Nearly 19.9 percent are 65 or older, so senior homestead rules matter a great deal in this county.

The county has four public school systems: Colbert County Schools, Muscle Shoals City, Sheffield City and Tuscumbia City. Which one applies depends on the address, so buyers should verify it. Terrain climbs from river bottom to ridge, putting one house near a floodplain and the next on a slope. If you live by the river or the rail corridor, be ready for questions about noise and flood status.

In Alabama a homestead means a single-family, owner-occupied dwelling with up to 160 acres of land. You qualify by owning the house and making it your primary residence as of the first day of the tax year in question.

WhoWhat is exemptWhere to claim
Owners over 65State portion of the property taxLocal tax office
Permanently and totally disabled ownersState portion of the property taxLocal tax office
Blind ownersState portion of the property taxLocal tax office
Manufactured home owners over 65Registration fee on an owner-occupied homeLocal tax office

The exemption covers the state share only, so county taxes may still be due. Manufactured home owners still pay the $5 issuance fee. Because roughly one in five residents is 65 or older, plenty of sellers here already hold an exemption. Notify the tax office when you sell. The buyer must file a new application.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
One mill equals a tenth of a cent. The bill comes from multiplying assessed value by the millage rate, and assessed value is a set percentage of appraised value. Your parcel's county, city and school district each contribute to the rate, so equal houses can carry unequal bills.

Two things push a bill up: a vote or board decision to raise the millage rate, or a higher appraised value on the property.

Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. If no statement reaches you, the obligation is the same. Call the tax office if you move or inherit a house, so statements go to an address you actually check.

Some transfers owe nothing. Under section 40-22-1 of the Alabama Code, three kinds are exempt: deeds given for nominal consideration to perfect a real estate title, corrected deeds that are recorded again, and mortgage transfers where the mortgage tax has already been paid.

All other deeds pay 50 cents per $500 of value, with proof of the real price or value handed to the recorder. If none arrives, the office uses the latest assessment. A person who deliberately holds back proof after being asked faces a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is larger.

An heir fixing a family title should ask the probate office about the nominal-consideration route before signing anything.

sections.h2: Selling a Colbert County house with taxes due
sections.html:
Yes, we can purchase a Colbert County house that is behind on tax. Whatever is owed after December 31 is typically paid from the sale proceeds, and we review the balance with you before making an offer.

  1. Call the tax office and ask for the amount owed on each tax year.
  2. Check whether you hold a homestead exemption and tell the office about the sale.
  3. Collect the deed, the latest bill and, for an inherited house, the probate paperwork.
  4. Ask the title company to confirm every payoff in writing.

Because no lender or appraisal is involved, you do not need to repair the house or pay the balance beforehand. Have the parcel number ready on our first call and we will pull up the account with you.

sections.h2: Questions to settle before you sign
sections.html:
Sellers get into trouble over small things: a deed with a name spelled two ways, a bill sent to an old address, or an owner's exemption that nobody canceled. Look over each of these before closing. Compare the name on your deed with your identification. Confirm that the mailing address on file with the county is one you read. Ask whether an exemption is attached to the parcel and who must close it out.

If the property was in a family for generations, add one more step. Old deeds near the eastern county line may carry an outdated boundary reference, because the line moved to Town Creek in 1890. Mention that to the title company so it can check the legal description. A short call now costs far less than a delay on closing day, and it lets you see what is owed before an offer is on the table.

One more habit helps. Photograph the house inside and out before you hand over keys, and keep the pictures with your closing papers. If a question ever comes up about the condition you left it in, you will have a dated record. Sellers who stay organized tend to finish faster, and they rarely have to chase a missing page or a forgotten receipt on the last day and with fewer phone calls, whether the buyer is a neighbor, an investor or us.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in the Shoals
sections.html:
Once you agree on a price, a title company or attorney opens the file. It searches the record for liens and old mortgages, asks the tax office for payoffs and drafts the deed. You sign, the funds move, and the deed is filed with the probate office. The probate office handles the recording.

What a cash sale leaves out is the lender. No bank order for an appraisal, no underwriting queue and no buyer financing that falls through a week before closing. What it cannot skip is the title work, so the earlier you start it, the sooner you close.

Plan for these items on closing day: a photo ID, the keys and openers, and any documents the title company requested. If you hold a homestead exemption or an owner's exemption on a manufactured home, mention it at the table so the paperwork reflects the change in ownership and the county knows to stop applying it. After closing, keep a copy of the settlement statement with your tax records.

faqs.q: What is the largest city in Colbert County, Alabama?
faqs.a: Muscle Shoals is the largest city. Tuscumbia is the county seat.

faqs.q: How many people live in Colbert County?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 57,227 people, and the 2025 estimate is 59,474.

faqs.q: Do people over 65 pay property tax in Colbert County?
faqs.a: They are exempt from the state portion if they claim the homestead exemption, but county taxes may still be due. File the claim at the local tax office.

faqs.q: What is a mill on an Alabama tax bill?
faqs.a: A mill is one-tenth of one cent, and the bill is the assessed value times the millage rate.

faqs.q: Will you buy a Colbert County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: We can. Delinquent taxes after December 31 are normally settled out of the sale proceeds, and we will go over the balance with you before making an offer.
